prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text: The provision for credit losses, which includes the provisions for loan credit losses, off-balance sheet commitments credit losses and security credit losses, is based on management’s assessment of the adequacy of our allowance for credit losses (“ACL”) for loans, securities, and our reserve for off-balance-sheet lending commitments. Factors impacting the provision include inherent risk characteristics in our loan and security portfolios, the level of nonperforming loans and net charge-offs, both current and historic, local economic and credit conditions, the direction of the change in collateral values, reasonable and supportable forecasts, and the funding probability on unfunded lending commitments. The provision for credit losses is charged against earnings in order to maintain our ACL, which reflects management’s best estimate of the life of loan/investment security credit losses inherent in our loan/security portfolios at the balance sheet date, and our reserve for off-balance-sheet lending commitments, which reflects management’s best estimate of losses inherent in our legally binding lending-related commitments. The allowance is increased by the provision for loan credit losses and decreased by charge-offs, net of recoveries.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents the significant components of noninterest expense for the periods indicated:

Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased by $461,000, or 0.7%, to $62.5 million, compared to $62.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to an increase of $2.7 million in salaries and employee benefits. The increase was offset by decreases of $1.4 million and $526,000 in other expense and electronic banking, respectively.

Salaries and employee benefits. The $2.7 million increase in salaries and employee benefits was primarily due to a $1.6 million increase in incentive compensation expense, including a $1.4 million increase in bonuses driven by improved performance. Also contributing to the increase was a net increase in salaries of $1.4 million primarily due to annual merit increases and a net increase of 6 full-time equivalent (“FTE”) employees.

Other noninterest expense . The $1.4 million decrease in other noninterest expense was primarily due to a $2.2 million release of litigation reserve which was offset by an $883,000 charge, both of which relate to the settlement of certain litigation involving the questioned banker activity first disclosed during the quarter ended June 30, 2024.

Electronic banking .

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $95.1 million, an increase of $11.4 million, or 13.7%, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was due to a $7.5 million decrease in interest expense and an increase of $3.9 million in total interest income during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to three months ended September 30, 2025.

The $7.5 million decrease in interest expense was mainly due to decreases of $6.9 million and $892,000 in interest expense on interest-bearing deposits and subordinated indebtedness, respectively. Of the $6.9 million decline in interest on interest-bearing deposits, $8.7 million was attributable to lower interest rates, partially offset by a $1.7 million net increase resulting from higher net average balances, during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $8.7 million decrease in interest expense due to lower rates was primarily due to decreases of $5.6 million and $2.2 million in interest expense on money market and interest-bearing demand deposits, respectively.

Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, decreased by $8.0 million to $18.1 million, compared to $26.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by a $7.0 million decrease in the change in fair value of equity investments, a $1.9 million decrease in other income, and a decrease of $985,000 in swap fee income. These decreases were partially offset by increases of $737,000 and $509,000 in insurance commission and fee income and equity method investment income, respectively.

Change in fair value of equity investments. The decrease of $7.0 million in the change of fair value of equity investments was primarily due to a fair value adjustment during the three months ended September 30, 2025, associated with our additional investment in Argent Financial. Our additional investment during the three months ended September 30, 2025, increased our ownership percentage above the threshold required to apply the equity method of accounting, which required the investment to be recorded at fair value immediately prior to the additional investment.

intro.text: Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to “we,” “us,” “our,” “our company,” “the Company” or “Origin” refer to Origin Bancorp, Inc., a Louisiana corporation, and its consolidated subsidiaries. All references to “Origin Bank” or “the Bank” refer to Origin Bank, our wholly-owned bank subsidiary. Origin Bancorp, Inc. is a financial holding company headquartered in Ruston, Louisiana. Our wholly owned bank subsidiary, Origin Bank, was founded in 1912 in Choudrant, Louisiana. Deeply rooted in our history is a culture committed to providing personalized, relationship banking to businesses, municipalities, and personal clients to enrich the lives of the people in the communities we serve.
